scenario: UGC community search for posts, questions and comments; prioritize relevance (nDCG), CTR, semantic matching, query understanding, recall, ranking and LLM applications.

papers.title: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval
papers.authors: Jinming Nian, Jyun-Yu Jiang, Henry Tsai, Yi Fang, Zhirong Liang
papers.summary: An LLM evolves executable semantic-index programs while a tiny retriever screens them. With the target training recipe fixed, NQ320K Recall@100 rises from 85.82% to 90.57%.
papers.key_insight: Index construction and collision handling are coupled. A cheap proxy can rank index changes well, yet become misleading when the search also changes the generator objective.

papers.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
papers.authors: He Ma, Lan You, Qiyang Wu, Chen Liu
papers.summary: LightCRS caches frozen multimodal product representations offline and uses a shared query-conditioned module to compare candidates online. HR@1 improves by 35.4% over the strongest baseline.
papers.key_insight: Separate reusable product evidence from dialogue-dependent matching. Query-conditioned fusion enables a compact shared model to serve multiple domains.

papers.title: Factual Access States in Diffusion Language Models: From Mechanism to Knowledge Editing and Retrieval
papers.authors: Yuchen Guo, Zhuoyuan Mao, Yiwen Guo
papers.summary: The paper identifies relation-dependent factual access states in diffusion LMs and uses them for editing and retrieval. Dream-7B reverse-QA accuracy on BAKE rises from 20.3% to 83.6%.
papers.key_insight: A fact occupies a region of internal states across paraphrases and directions. Editing that region generalizes better than editing a single prompt state.

papers.title: Self-Credit: Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agentic RL via Intra-group Rescaling
papers.authors: Fangcong Yin, Ming Yin, Tanvi Bhandarkar, Aashu Singh, Eryk Helenowski
papers.summary: Self-Credit asks agents to cite useful earlier actions and rescales that credit across successful and failed rollouts. On BrowseComp-Plus the 8B model beats the strongest agentic RL baseline by 8.5 points.
papers.key_insight: Self-reported credit needs cross-rollout checks. Comparing success and failure helps distinguish frequently cited actions from actions that support the answer.

papers.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
papers.authors: Qian Xie, Wenyue Hua, Yueli He, Sripad Karne, Armaan Agrawal, Nikos Pagonas, Eugene Wu, Kostis Kaffes, Tianyi Peng, Nairen Cao
papers.summary: CC-Gittins searches model assignments for complete agent workflows while accounting for quality and deployment cost. Across eight benchmarks it recovers a substantial part of the Pareto frontier at roughly 10% of exhaustive evaluation cost.
papers.key_insight: Evaluate assignments end to end. Coupled evaluation and deployment costs let each trial inform both quality-seeking and cost-seeking searches.

papers.title: DiffuPlan: Editable Planning State for Diffusion Language Model Agents
papers.authors: Qisheng Zhou, Zhen Xiong, Qiaoyu Tan
papers.summary: DiffuPlan maintains editable planning state and reconstructs affected steps when search evidence changes. It reaches 50.24 average F1 across four multi-hop QA benchmarks.
papers.key_insight: Treat a plan as revisable state. Local reconstruction can replace obsolete hypotheses instead of accumulating corrections in an append-only history.

papers.title: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning: Laws and Synthesis Strategies
papers.authors: Bowei He, Yankai Chen, Xiaokun Zhang, Changjiang Han, Ye Yuan, Chong Li, Xue Liu
papers.summary: The paper separates agentic training data into task, environment and trajectory counts, plus reward density, and studies scaling across models and domains using PPO and GRPO.
papers.key_insight: Data volume hides coverage. Track the cost of new tasks, new environments and repeated trajectories separately; the recommendation connection is a proposed transfer, not an evaluated result.

papers.title: BERT Is Already a Denoiser: Cheaply Unlocking Iterative Generation in Masked Language Models
papers.summary: An iterative confidence-based decoder turns masked LMs into conditional generators without diffusion training. Ordinary MLM adaptation brings BERT to 28.2% on ARC-Easy.
papers.key_insight: Denoising pretraining, task adaptation and commitment scheduling play distinct roles. Frozen reconstruction ability alone does not establish task-directed generation.

papers.title: Training the Whole Agent, Not Just the Model
papers.authors: Lingxiao Tang, Wei Tao, Yiwen Guo, Lingfeng Bao
papers.summary: HarnessAdapt-RL updates both the policy and its tools during reinforcement learning. With a 9B model it improves SWE-bench Verified pass@1 by 9.8 percentage points over GRPO.
papers.key_insight: The deployment artifact is a model–harness pair. Temporary skills can be removed, but evolved tools and hooks remain part of the learned system.

papers.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
papers.authors: Xialie Zhuang, Mingcong Lei, Zunhai Su, Ri Liu, Jianjin Li
papers.summary: DecisionPivot evaluates decision correctness, probability ordering and confidence with controlled contrast groups. Two similarly ranked models score 70.1% and 44.2% contrast-group accuracy.
papers.key_insight: Score related cases together. A model can rank probabilities well while making inconsistent decisions when a decisive detail changes.
